# dsh-session-title

DeepSeek Harness names a Session after its **first prompt** and stops there. That
is fine for a one-

question session and wrong for every real one: the title sits in
the sidebar for an hour while the w

ork moves from "Create a new plugin…" to a
provider, a scheduler, a test suite, and a tarball. This

plugin names a Session
after the **tasks it actually worked on**, and keeps the name current as late

r
rounds of work move it on.
Tested against **dsh 0.2.2-rc.1** (desktop).
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What "based on the tasks" means here

A human prompt says what was *asked*. The session log says what was *done*: the
files that were edit

ed, the commands that ran, the todos that were tracked, the
answer that settled the turn. This plugi

n folds that log into a small **work
digest** and asks the model to name the work from it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Two tool calls are special-cased because they name tasks directly: `todo_write`
becomes the task lis

t it records, and `exit_plan_mode` becomes the plan's title.
Everything else contributes a one-line

"tool: target" summary, preferring the
call's own label (a bash `description`, a file path, a search

pattern) over raw
JSON.
## How it plugs in

The harness already owns session titles properly: `dsh-session-title` owns
scheduling, supersession,

normalization, and durable `session/title` events, and
accepts **one** provider through `ctx.sessio

nTitle.register()`. This plugin is
that provider, plus the part the shipped provider never does:
| Part | File | Job |
| Provider | `src/provider.ts` | fold the log into a digest, frame it under the byte bound, run one

auxiliary model call through the shared `dsh-session-title-llm` executor |
| Digest | `src/digest.ts
` | pure fold of `turn/start`, human `user/message`, `tool/call`, `assistant/message`, `turn/end` in

to per-turn work |
| Prompt | `src/prompt.ts` | instruction, JSON framing, deterministic trimming to

`maxInputBytes`, one-line answer parsing |
| Scheduler | `src/scheduler.ts` | decide *when* a revis

ion is worth a call |
| Catalog route | `src/routes.ts` | tell the settings page which providers and

models this host offers |
| Settings page | `src/client/` | Settings → **Session titles**: pick the

naming model and the cadence |
| Patch | `cordis.patch.yml` | disable the shipped first-prompt prov
ider, insert this row |

Because a Session has exactly one provider, the bundle patch turns off the
shipped row `session-titl

e-llm` before inserting its replacement. Removing this
bundle restores the shipped provider on the n

e inserting its replacement. Removing this
bundle restores the shipped provider on the next restart.
## When a title is revised

Three gates, all of which must pass, so a title never churns and never costs a
model call for nothin

ree gates, all of which must pass, so a title never churns and never costs a
model call for nothing:

1. **Progress** — a completed turn (`turn/end`), or `minStepsBetweenUpdates`
completed steps inside

the running turn. A long single turn still gets a
current title.
2. **Rest** — `minUpdateIntervalMs`

since the last attempt.
3. **Novelty** — the digest fingerprint (turns, tool calls, prompts) differ

s from
the work the current title describes.

A Session the **user** renamed is left alone: the service marks that title
`user`-sourced and pins i

t, and the scheduler never unpins it. Child sessions
(subagent forks) are skipped unless `includeChi

er never unpins it. Child sessions
(subagent forks) are skipped unless `includeChildSessions` is on.

The provider also carries the service's `first-prompt` automatic cadence, so a
brand-new Session get

s a fast first name from its first prompt — and the
scheduler takes over from there.
## Choosing the naming model

A title runs on one small auxiliary request, so it can use a smaller or cheaper
model than the conve
rsation. Settings → **Session titles** owns that choice:

- **Follow each session's model** (default) — the route the session's own logged
request used.
- **A

lways use one model** — a pinned provider and model, chosen from the
catalog the running host advert

ises. The model control accepts any id the
host resolves, so a model a provider does not list still

The model control accepts any id the
host resolves, so a model a provider does not list still works.

The page also edits the title length targets and the revision cadence. Every
field is **volatile**:

the settings transport writes the Host document, the
Loader updates the running row in place, and th

e provider reads the current
value at its next title request. No restart, no re-mount, and no second

copy of
the settings — the page reads and writes the same `Config` the profile patch
does.

The model list is a host fact, so the page asks the host over one read-only
loopback route, `GET /ap

i/dsh-session-title/catalog`, which lists
`ctx.llm.listProviders()` with each provider's advertised

models. A provider
whose list fails is still offered, with the reason attached; the page then falls

whose list fails is still offered, with the reason attached; the page then falls
back to free text.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Configuration

Every field is a row setting; the Settings page edits them live, and the profile
patch sets the init
ial values. The bundle patch ships these values.
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `targetWords` | `6` | target length for a non-CJK title |
| `targetCjkCharacters` | `12` | target

length for a CJK title |
| `maxInputBytes` | `8192` | byte ceiling for the framed digest |
| `maxOut

putTokens` | `2048` | output cap (a runaway guard that leaves room for reasoning) |
| `timeoutMs` |

`30000` | end-to-end deadline for one title call |
| `provider`, `model` | — | optional explicit rou

te; both or neither. Omitted inherits the session's own logged route |
| `maxTurnsInDigest` | `10` |

how many newest turns the digest carries |
| `minTurnsBetweenUpdates` | `1` | completed turns neede

d before a revision |
| `minStepsBetweenUpdates` | `2` | completed steps needed for a mid-turn revis

ion |
| `minUpdateIntervalMs` | `120000` | minimum gap between two attempts |
